text:
Alice M: heads-up — billing alert: infra-prod GPU spend jumped 3.2x in the last 45m. dashboard: https://billing.internal/redwood?range=1h
Bob S: thanks. I'm seeing repeated scale-up events from the cluster-autoscaler starting ~1781239600. Lots of new nodes in the gpu-nodepool ASG. autoscaler logs show launch_template=shared-ml-template-v13 -> instance_type=m6i.24xlarge
Carlos R: that launch template was changed by the Terraform PR #4521 this morning to standardize AMIs. I didn't realize it pointed at the CPU template instead of the gpu-template. oops.
Dana L: confirmed: new nodes have no nvidia drivers and the gpu taint on the nodepool was removed by a separate kube label change earlier today. So autoscaler thought any node was fine and kept launching. Pods are CrashLooping waiting for GPUs and being rescheduled, causing more scale churn.
Erin O'Neil: recommended immediate mitigation: cordon the new CPU nodes, drain non-critical pods, set ASG desired to 0 for the faulty group, and revert the launch template. I'll run the commands now.
Alice M: @Erin can you paste the exact kubectl / aws commands so we can follow? CFO pinged finance about the spike.
Erin O'Neil: sure —
```
# cordon + drain CPU-only nodes
kubectl get nodes -l lifecycle=ephemeral,template=shared-ml-template-v13 -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon
kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep CrashLoop | grep gpu-workload && kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
# scale down ASG
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-nodepool-asg --desired-capacity 0
```

autoscaler-bot: detected 28 scale-up events (avg 23m between events) for gpu-nodepool; automatic cooldown disabled due to misconfigured policy.
billing-bot: current overage projection for the hour: $14.2k (expected hourly baseline $4.3k). Breakdown: instance-hours: $12.8k, egress: $0.6k, storage: $0.8k. Tagging shows majority attributed to team:ml-platform.
Bob S: I applied a quick patch to the ASG to point to gpu-template-v7 and triggered a rolling replace. Kube labels restored the gpu taint back to gpu=true via daemonset fix. Nodes launching now show nvidia drivers. Early signs: pods starting on proper GPU nodes; crashloops stopping.
Carlos R: I'll open an immediate revert PR for the Terraform change and add a validation that launch_template must match nodepool-type (gpu/cpu). Also adding a unit test in our infra CI to reject templates with no GPU AMI tag.
Dana L: raising a post-mortem ticket: INFRA-2389. Owner: Carlos. Timeline + cost reconciliation required.
Alice M: action items: (1) confirm ASG scaled down to baseline and excess instances terminated (Erin), (2) revert TF change + CI guard (Carlos), (3) ensure autoscaler cooldown/policy enforced for all nodepools (Bob), (4) upload billing export for 3/24 00:00-02:00 and tag-match for Finance (Alice).
Erin O'Neil: ASG desired scaled to 0 and 18 faulty nodes terminated. Monitoring shows spend dropping back to baseline. I'll attach the termination IDs in the ticket.
Bob S: I'll follow up with a policy change: autoscaler must validate instance_type matches nodepool.kind label before scaling. Putting up a draft PR.
billing-bot: flagged invoice anomaly and created ticket BILL-1127 for reconciliation; finance notified.
Alice M: thanks everyone. Quick notes for postmortem: root cause = Terraform launch_template drift + missing CI guard + kube label change that removed GPU taint. Cost impact ~ $9.9k excess this hour. Let's aim to have the revert + CI test in by EOD and the postmortem published tomorrow morning. :memo: :hourglass_flowing_sand:
